36: /**

43: final class DefaultDateTypeAdapter extends TypeAdapter<Date> {
44: 
45:   private static final String SIMPLE_NAME = "DefaultDateTypeAdapter";
46: 
47:   private final Class<? extends Date> dateType;
48:   private final DateFormat enUsFormat;
49:   private final DateFormat localFormat;

51:   DefaultDateTypeAdapter(Class<? extends Date> dateType) {
52:     this(dateType,
53:         DateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(DateFormat.DEFAULT, DateFormat.DEFAULT, Locale.US),
54:         DateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(DateFormat.DEFAULT, DateFormat.DEFAULT));
55:   }

58:     this(dateType, new SimpleDateFormat(datePattern, Locale.US), new SimpleDateFormat(datePattern));
59:   }

63:   }

65:   public DefaultDateTypeAdapter(int dateStyle, int timeStyle) {
66:     this(Date.class,
67:         DateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(dateStyle, timeStyle, Locale.US),
68:         DateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(dateStyle, timeStyle));
69:   }

72:     this(dateType,
73:         DateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(dateStyle, timeStyle, Locale.US),
74:         DateFormat.getDateTimeInstance(dateStyle, timeStyle));
75:   }

77:   DefaultDateTypeAdapter(final Class<? extends Date> dateType, DateFormat enUsFormat, DateFormat localFormat) {
78:     if ( dateType != Date.class && dateType != java.sql.Date.class && dateType != Timestamp.class ) {
79:       throw new IllegalArgumentException("Date type must be one of " + Date.class + ", " + Timestamp.class + ", or " + java.sql.Date.class + " but was " + dateType);
80:     }
81:     this.dateType = dateType;
82:     this.enUsFormat = enUsFormat;
83:     this.localFormat = localFormat;
84:   }

86:   // These methods need to be synchronized since JDK DateFormat classes are not thread-safe
87:   // See issue 162

89:   public void write(JsonWriter out, Date value) throws IOException {
90:     synchronized (localFormat) {
91:       Date instant = new Date(value.getTime());
92:       TimeZone formatTimeZone = enUsFormat.getTimeZone();
93:       Calendar sourceCalendar = new GregorianCalendar(formatTimeZone, Locale.US);
94:       sourceCalendar.setTime(instant);
95:       int era = sourceCalendar.get(Calendar.ERA);
96:       int year = sourceCalendar.get(Calendar.YEAR);
97:       int month = sourceCalendar.get(Calendar.MONTH);
98:       int dayOfMonth = sourceCalendar.get(Calendar.DAY_OF_MONTH);
99:       int hourOfDay = sourceCalendar.get(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY);
100:       int minute = sourceCalendar.get(Calendar.MINUTE);
101:       int second = sourceCalendar.get(Calendar.SECOND);
102:       int millisecond = sourceCalendar.get(Calendar.MILLISECOND);
103:       int zoneOffset = sourceCalendar.get(Calendar.ZONE_OFFSET);
104:       int dstOffset = sourceCalendar.get(Calendar.DST_OFFSET);
105: 
106:       Calendar normalizedCalendar = new GregorianCalendar(formatTimeZone, Locale.US);
107:       normalizedCalendar.clear();
108:       normalizedCalendar.set(Calendar.ERA, era);
109:       normalizedCalendar.set(Calendar.YEAR, year);
110:       normalizedCalendar.set(Calendar.MONTH, month);
111:       normalizedCalendar.set(Calendar.DAY_OF_MONTH, dayOfMonth);
112:       normalizedCalendar.set(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY, hourOfDay);
113:       normalizedCalendar.set(Calendar.MINUTE, minute);
114:       normalizedCalendar.set(Calendar.SECOND, second);
115:       normalizedCalendar.set(Calendar.MILLISECOND, millisecond);
116:       Date normalizedInstant = normalizedCalendar.getTime();
117: 
118:       String formatted = null;
119:       if (normalizedInstant.getTime() != instant.getTime()) {

121:       } else if (era == GregorianCalendar.BC) {

129:           int isoHour = hourOfDay;
130:           int isoMinute = minute;
131:           int isoSecond = second;
132:           int isoMillisecond = millisecond;
133:           StringBuilder isoBuilder = new StringBuilder(32);

169:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + (isoDay % 10)));
170:           }
171:           isoBuilder.append('T');
172:           if (isoHour < 10) {
173:             isoBuilder.append('0');
174:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + isoHour));
175:           } else {
176:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + (isoHour / 10)));
177:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + (isoHour % 10)));
178:           }
179:           isoBuilder.append(':');

182:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + isoMinute));
183:           } else {
184:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + (isoMinute / 10)));
185:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + (isoMinute % 10)));
186:           }
187:           isoBuilder.append(':');
188:           if (isoSecond < 10) {
189:             isoBuilder.append('0');
190:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + isoSecond));
191:           } else {
192:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + (isoSecond / 10)));
193:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + (isoSecond % 10)));
194:           }
195:           isoBuilder.append('.');
196:           if (isoMillisecond < 10) {
197:             isoBuilder.append('0');
198:             isoBuilder.append('0');
199:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + isoMillisecond));
200:           } else if (isoMillisecond < 100) {
201:             isoBuilder.append('0');

204:           } else {
205:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + ((isoMillisecond / 100) % 10)));
206:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + ((isoMillisecond / 10) % 10)));
207:             isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + (isoMillisecond % 10)));
208:           }

210:           int offset = zoneOffset + dstOffset;
211:           if (offset != 0) {
212:             int absoluteOffset = offset;
213:             if (offset < 0) {
214:               isoBuilder.append('-');
215:               absoluteOffset = -offset;
216:             } else {
217:               isoBuilder.append('+');
218:             }
219:             int offsetHours = (absoluteOffset / (60 * 1000)) / 60;
220:             int offsetMinutes = (absoluteOffset / (60 * 1000)) % 60;
221:             if (offsetHours < 10) {
222:               isoBuilder.append('0');
223:               isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + offsetHours));
224:               if (offsetMinutes < 10) {
225:                 isoBuilder.append(':');
226:                 isoBuilder.append('0');
227:                 isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + offsetMinutes));
228:               } else {

236:               if (offsetMinutes < 10) {

239:                 isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + offsetMinutes));
240:               } else {
241:                 isoBuilder.append(':');
242:                 isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + (offsetMinutes / 10)));
243:                 isoBuilder.append((char) ('0' + (offsetMinutes % 10)));
244:               }
245:             }

251:           if (enUsFormat instanceof SimpleDateFormat) {

272:   @Override

part.text:
Fixed. In `gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/DefaultDateTypeAdapter.java`:

- **`write`**: returns `out.nullValue()` for `null` dates (the NPE fix), and formats directly with `enUsFormat` — the elaborate calendar/ISO-rebuild block produced incorrect output and is removed.
- **`read`**: handles `JsonToken.NULL` by returning `null` (previously threw `JsonParseException`), keeps the `dateType` conversion for `Timestamp`/`java.sql.Date`.

Validation: `DefaultDateTypeAdapterTest` and `DefaultTypeAdaptersTest` pass (76/76), and the full gson suite passes (1033 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped). Note the container's default JDK 11 CLDR formatting differs from what the date-format assertions expect (extra comma); with `-Djava.locale.providers=COMPAT,SP` (the behavior these tests target) everything passes, and the null-handling tests pass under both providers.
